flaws: The page 4 footer sits lower than on other pages and the cover illustration's tree clips the page edge.
Page 4 is crowded and its footer sits lower than on the other pages, with some fine print that looks under 11 pt.
The wrench and loop arrow are awkwardly fused off-axis, and the wrench shrinks to a blob at 16 px.
The wrench head is jammed onto the loop with a stubby neck, so at 32 and 16 px it collapses into an unreadable squiggle, and it too is barely visible on dark.
The hermit crab sits low and cramped in the pool, and the large gap above the buttons leaves the stacked actions slightly detached from the content.
The results sheet covers most of the finished pool, so the 'shown over the pool' moment is reduced to a strip at the top.
Slide 2 shows only opening times with a confusing Closes column (Thursday's old 7 pm closing is missing), and its small legend and headers are hard to read from the back.
On slide 2 the column labels and the legend are small caps around 27-30 px, borderline against the 28 px floor, and Thursday's old closing time is never shown.
The amber lamp disc sits over the arm pivot in the front view, partly hiding the arm root.
From the front the amber lamp sits in front of the pivot and hides the boss, and the arm reads short, so the raised-arm silhouette is weaker than the lamp.
Cart is cramped with a small pot and faint steam, and the tile's mortar network looks somewhat busy and uniform when repeated.
The steam wisps look pale and possibly semi-transparent, and the lantern reads more as painted than truly lit.
The Snooze control is a borderless text link, so its 56 pt tap area is not visible and it sits close to Cancel.
Snooze has no visible button boundary, so its 56 pt hit area and its gap from Cancel can't be checked by eye.
The dimmed '00:' hours in the clock and the many small grey labels around it make the take in progress slightly harder to read at a glance and the panel feels busy.
The dimmed '00:' hours segment and busy waveform slightly dilute the clock's punch compared with a single solid readout.
Small body text on the first-month and seasons pages looks close to the 11 pt floor and the cover is fairly busy.
Supporting text on the checklist and Who to ask cards looks smaller than 11 pt, and the cover illustration is plain and boxy.
The lamp housing is oversized and overlaps the arm base, and the counterweight lever is a tiny nub that barely reads.
The lamp housing is oversized and bulges well past the post in plan, and the counterweight lever is so small it barely registers.
The 'Cancel alarm' label runs into its button border, and the button sits right beside Snooze with only a plain tap to trigger it.
The 'Cancel alarm' label is crammed against its button's right edge, and the stop-line timeline overruns the right margin.
Slide 2 table text, column headers and footers are small for a projector across a long room.
The footer text and the small labels look about 24 px, under the 28 px floor and hard to read from the back of a long room.
The shells are uneven in size and the empty one is a vague dashed blob, and the dark Replay button sits above the cream Next pool, which makes the hierarchy less clear.
A stray translucent square sits behind the crab, and the outlined Replay button on the dark water reads weaker than the rest.
The progress bar has an unexplained grey block and the info on the right of the panel is thin, so the area feels a little empty.
The best take's row gets only a small badge with no row highlight, and the toolbar is sparse, so the lower half feels plainer and less studio-specific.
Cat and cart use dark brown outlines that sink into the plum background, and the cobble tile reads as a brick-like wall with visible horizontal banding when repeated.
The ground tile reads as regular coursed stone blocks rather than cobblestones, and the cart's steam is lost under the awning.
The wrench head is a blunt block that reads a little like a plug, and the dark green is low contrast on the dark ground.
The dark green nearly disappears on the dark ground, and the U-shaped body risks reading as the letter U or a magnet.
